scenes.script_line: A new story becomes real when you start living it. Thinking changes feelings. Feelings change actions. And consistent actions change your life. In step nine, you'll design specific actions that become lifestyle rituals, so your new story can become your reality. Why rituals, and not just goals? Because a goal is something you reach once. A ritual is something you repeat, until it becomes part of who you are.

scenes.script_line: On page nineteen, you'll create three to five rituals that support your new story. Then you'll check each one against a simple test called AIMS. A is for aligns. Does this ritual align with what matters most to you, and your forward-moving goals? I is for invest. Can you invest between forty-five and ninety days in making it part of your lifestyle? That's a real commitment. So choose rituals you're genuinely willing to keep, not ones that only sound impressive today. M is for measurable. scenes.script_line: One simple way to make a ritual stick is to attach it to something you already do. After I pour my morning coffee, I read my new story. Before I leave work, I note one thing I did that fits it. Existing habits become reminders for the new ones. Here are two of Sam's rituals. "Every weekday morning, I read my new story out loud before I open my email." "In every team meeting, I share at least one idea in the first fifteen minutes." Both are small. Both are measurable. And both build evidence for the new story, day after day.

scenes.script_line: That's the hidden power of rituals. Every time you do one, you prove the new story a little more true. And the old story gets a little quieter. A common mistake is making rituals too big. If a ritual won't survive a busy week, make it smaller. Small and consistent beats big and occasional. Think across your life as you choose. One ritual might be about your mindset, like reading your story. Another might be about your relationships, like having one honest conversation a week.
